prize_count_note: 28 non-cash prizes listed on Devpost; the entries above are the ones with stated criteria or notable shape.

criteria.label: WOW factor
criteria.description: Stands out and leaves a lasting impression; achieves its goal exceptionally in any dimension.

criteria.label: Technical ability
criteria.description: Technical depth and advanced knowledge rated favorably.

criteria.label: Originality
criteria.description: New problem, new approach, or something unique even if it solves no problem.

criteria.label: Design
criteria.description: User-friendly, intuitive and engaging for its audience.

judging.judge_profile_summary: 31 judges: founders/CEOs of startups, CTOs and heads of engineering/product, two Y Combinator partners/staff, VC partners, a design leader, a robotics VP and an online personality. Heavy founder/builder weighting.
judging.notes: WOW factor is listed first in both the main rubric and several sponsor rubrics (Cohere, Warp).

sources.note: Dates, participants, prizes, judges, judging criteria.
Team size: up to 4 members, all present in person.
All 11 pages captured: 261 submissions counted, 260 publicly listed. Winner ribbons mark every prize-winning project.
2026 site features S-KBD67, ROSS and DUM-E as past projects.

curator_notes: Roster captured from the Devpost gallery on 2026-10-12: Devpost counts 261 submissions and lists 260 publicly (page 3 shows 23 items on repeated fetches). Prize names come from each winning project page (54 projects carry a Winner ribbon: the 12 finalists and 42 sponsor-prize winners). Projects holding both a finalist spot and a sponsor prize take the higher-weight status (track-winner) with both awards listed. All 54 prize winners are analyzed records (2026-10-13). Taglines are CrafterWIKI paraphrases; domains were assigned conservatively and left empty for 25 entries whose gallery text does not say what they do. Sponsor prizes with 1st/2nd/3rd tiers (e.g. Cohere) do not show the tier on project pages, so ranks are not recorded.
